ai.description: *Megophrys vegrandis* is a small toad (25–30 mm) with brown dorsal coloration and dark markings. It is distinguished by a prominent, triangular skin projection on each upper eyelid.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys vegrandis* is best distinguished from similar Indian congeners by its notably small adult size and the presence of a distinct, elongated, horn-like tubercle on each upper eyelid.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys vegrandis* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests of the Eastern Himalayas, typically found near streams at elevations ranging from 2,000 to 2,700 meters.
ai.behavior: *Megophrys vegrandis* is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter during the day to ambush small invertebrate prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys vegrandis* breeds in streams during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys vegrandis* is endemic to the high-elevation forests of the Eastern Himalayas in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, typically occurring above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: *Megophrys vegrandis* emits a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard emanating from small, rocky streams within montane forests.
